recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future work on `Bundle/uscore-mo3` or similar US Core example validation should be directed to the applicable US Core IG or validator/tooling repository, not the FHIR core specification checkout.
issue_request: FHIR-12495 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU2 FHIR-core tracker reporting that IG Publisher QA was not validating the US Core `Bundle/uscore-mo3` bundled example correctly. The Jira application comment says the profile declarations were incorrect and were fixed in GitHub.
initial_application: No FHIR core commit explicitly mentions FHIR-12495, and current core source does not contain `uscore-mo3`. The matching application is HL7/US-Core-STU3 commit 41a2ef775f5ac9a9b3649d8db9580cad6e3cc962, `fix wrong profile declarations`, which edits only `examples/uscore-mo3.xml` by deleting the Bundle-level profile declaration and correcting the bundled MedicationRequest profile declaration.
additional_context: The Zulip #committers IG Publisher thread records Eric Haas raising the bundled-example QA concern and then tagging GF#12495 to Grahame. Current `source/fhir.ini` comments out the old `us-core` profile entry, and current source searches found no FHIR-12495 or uscore-mo3 source. FHIR-15757 was considered only as background because it is a later, separate bundle/profile validator issue.
reconciliation: Published an empty external-repo audit commit on the combined branch. No current FHIR core source was changed because the applied fix belongs to the external US Core STU3 IG repository and the affected old US Core source is not active in the current core build.
